issues.legal_issue: A delay in applying to set aside an ex parte decree may be condoned when the explanation is acceptable and the circumstances support advancing substantial justice.
material_facts: The application to set aside the ex parte decree was filed 554 days late.

The appellant said he did not learn of the decree until receiving notice of execution proceedings and that the person who had appeared for the company had left after his son died, without informing him of later proceedings.
The Court considered the appellant insufficiently vigilant but not so irresponsible that he should be excluded from litigation over valuable property.
The inconvenience to the respondent from the delay could be compensated by exemplary costs.
issues.conclusion: The delay was condoned, subject to payment of exemplary costs to the respondent.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 5 of the Limitation Act, the court has discretion to admit an application after the prescribed period where sufficient cause is shown; that discretion should be exercised to advance substantial justice. The explanation’s acceptability, rather than the length of delay, is the principal criterion, and delay should generally be condoned absent gross negligence, deliberate inaction, or lack of bona fides. The Court relied on Ramlal v. Rewa Coalfields Ltd., The State of West Bengal v. The Administrator, Howrah Municipality, G. Ramegowda v. Special Land Acquisition Officer, and N. Balakrishnan v. M. Krishnamurthy.

rule.if: application_to_set_aside_ex_parte_decree and delay_in_filing and (acceptable_explanation or valuable_property_stake) and not deliberate_or_grossly_negligent_delay and delay_prejudice_compensable_by_costs

predicates.application_to_set_aside_ex_parte_decree: The defendant applied to set aside a decree entered when the defendant did not appear at the hearing.
predicates.delay_in_filing: The defendant filed that application after the applicable filing period had expired.
predicates.acceptable_explanation: The defendant gave an explanation for not filing the application within the prescribed period that the court found acceptable.
predicates.valuable_property_stake: The litigation concerned property the court regarded as valuable and involving a significant stake for the parties.
predicates.deliberate_or_grossly_negligent_delay: The party’s delay resulted from deliberate inaction, gross negligence, or lack of bona fides.
predicates.delay_prejudice_compensable_by_costs: The inconvenience caused to the opposing party by the delay could be compensated by an award of costs.
predicates.delay_condoned_subject_to_costs: The court admits the late application on the condition that the applicant pay costs.

issues.definition: When a late application to set aside an ex parte decree has an acceptable explanation or concerns a valuable property stake, is not attributable to deliberate or grossly negligent delay, and its prejudice can be compensated by costs, the delay is condoned subject to costs.

issues.legal_issue: An ex parte decree should be set aside when sufficient cause prevented the defendant from appearing when the suit was heard.
material_facts: The appellant said he was unaware of the decree until he received notice of execution proceedings.
The person who had appeared for the company had left after his son died, and the appellant said nobody informed him of the later proceedings.
The appellant applied to set aside the decree after learning of it.
The Court examined the application on its merits and found sufficient grounds to set aside the decree.
issues.conclusion: The application to set aside the ex parte decree was allowed, subject to payment of exemplary costs; otherwise the appeal would be deemed dismissed and the decree revived.
issues.legal_principle: The governing sufficient-cause standard for setting aside an ex parte decree is that the defendant must satisfy the court that sufficient cause prevented appearance when the suit was called for hearing. The Court applied that standard and found sufficient grounds on the facts presented.

predicates.application_to_set_aside_ex_parte_decree: The defendant applied to set aside a decree entered when the defendant did not appear at the hearing.
predicates.defendant_prevented_from_appearing_by_su: Circumstances the court accepts as sufficient prevented the defendant from appearing when the suit was heard.
predicates.ex_parte_decree_set_aside: The court sets aside the decree entered in the defendant’s absence.

issues.definition: If a defendant applies to set aside an ex parte decree and sufficient cause prevented the defendant from appearing at the hearing, the decree is set aside.
